newsitem.title: FRANCE: Algeria increases tax harvest by 59 pct in 1996.
newsitem.headline: Algeria increases tax harvest by 59 pct in 1996.

text.p: Algeria increased its direct tax collecting by 59.5 percent to 36.7 billion dinars ($658 million) in 1996 from 23 billion dinars in 1995, the official Algerian news agency APS said, quoting government data.

APS said the rise in the tax collection came from a tighter government policy set early in 1996 to stem tax evasion. The government set up a cross-ministries taskforce in 1996 to fight tax cheating and improve coordination between customs and tax collectors.

Officials said the recovered tax would be devoted to stemming poverty and other social woes which the authorities argue drove many disgruntled young people into the arms of radical Moslem fundamentalists.
About 60,000 people have been killed in Algeria's conflict since early 1992 when the authorities cancelled a general election in which militant Islamists had taken a huge lead.
